title: Speed Reading
coreMove: Remove the friction that slows reading while matching speed to comprehension demands.
sourcePressure: Reading efficiency is treated as cleaner pacing, reduced regressions, and preserved comprehension rather than careless skimming.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Equating speed reading with skimming or status performance.
sourceAnchorNote: Frozen sidecar contains no chapter-local named figure, named study, named place, or dated anecdote. Use fictional protagonists and keep source alignment at the concept and title-pressure level.

hook: Do not open Speed Reading with a generic unlocked potential claim.
Do not start with a definition of speed reading.
counterintuition: Do not use a not X but Y correction shell.
Do not claim the opposite of common sense in generic coaching language.
tryThisNow: Do not use set a timer and reflect.
Do not ask the reader to journal broadly without a visible action.
examples: No repeated desk, kitchen, classroom, commute, or generic meeting shells.
No six examples built around timestamp plus named protagonist plus decision.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: nurse practitioner reading dense trials efficiently
exampleSpecs.stakes: clinic protocol discussion starts at noon
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ruth runs a finger pace through the methods section, marks regressions, and slows only at the outcome table.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a printed trial with the outcome table boxed

exampleSpecs.audience: inventor scanning prior art without missing key claims
exampleSpecs.stakes: a filing deadline is six days away
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You preview claim headings, pace through known boilerplate, and stop fully when a claim overlaps your design.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a patent claim page covered in tiny numbers

exampleSpecs.audience: analyst reading hundreds of resident comments
exampleSpecs.stakes: council summary must preserve minority concerns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Diego sorts comments by signal first, then slows for representative objections instead of rereading every sentence twice.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: comment pages clipped in stacks of twenty

exampleSpecs.audience: assistant reading descriptions for provenance clues
exampleSpecs.stakes: a misread note can misprice an archive item
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anke uses clean pacing on standard fields and pauses when marginalia or ownership marks appear.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cotton gloves beside a catalog card

exampleSpecs.domain: sales contract review for a solar installer
exampleSpecs.audience: operations manager reading boilerplate and exceptions
exampleSpecs.stakes: install date depends on spotting one financing clause
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Michael identifies where regressions waste time, then reads standard clauses faster while flagging unusual financing language.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a financing clause highlighted in green

exampleSpecs.audience: student tempted to speed through every paragraph equally
exampleSpecs.stakes: discussion grade depends on understanding the hard argument
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lea asks which paragraphs deserve speed and which deserve wrestling, then changes pace at each argumentative turn.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a margin note shaped like a question mark

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm, using a question to the reader, a research aside only if source-supported, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: Identify when remove the friction that slows reading while matching speed to comprehension demands. is needed in a new scenario.
Choose the visible action that matches Speed Reading rather than a nearby generic lesson.
Explain why the weak alternative fails without using recall-only phrasing.

tryThisNowSpec: Preview the next page, choose where to speed up and where to slow down, then read with that pacing on purpose.
